outcomes: Checks who can capture the forking piece on its square and whether the capture costs the capturer more
Predicts how one added piece turns a working fork into a failing one
Notices when an added piece does not matter
sources: L-TAC-FORK-1 and L-TAC-FORK-2 (taught there, not repeated)
Lichess puzzle database (CC0): oSH1C, JHfLu, jT1B2, Hp6R3

steps.text: You know **Forks: one move, two targets** and **Forks with pawns and queens, and when they fail**. Now count the forking square. Ask who can capture the forking piece, what that capture costs them, and whether you can recapture. A fork wins material only if every reply loses something. Change one feature of a fork and predict again.

steps.caption: White to move. One knight move hits the king and the rook.

line.say: The knight gives check and attacks the rook on b3. The king guards d4.
The king steps away. The rook is still attacked.

claims.statement: Nd4+ wins the rook for nothing along the engine line.

steps.text: On the forking square, count the captures. If a black piece can capture your forking piece and you cannot recapture, the fork fails, whatever the capturer is worth. If you can recapture, compare what each side gives up. **Rule of thumb:** with counting values 3 for a knight and 5 for a rook, a knight traded for a rook gains. Recount after every change.

steps.title: The forking square
steps.prompt: Only one black piece differs from the first position. Predict whether Nf7+ wins material.
In the position that took you longest, which first move did you consider, and why did it fail? Name the forking square you chose, then rate how sure you were (low / medium / high).

steps.text: **Remember.** A fork wins material only if every reply loses something. On the forking square, ask who can capture your forking piece and whether you can recapture. If they can capture and you cannot recapture, the fork fails. If you can recapture, compare what each side gives up. Recount after every change.
